title: BRIDGING PSYCHOMETRIC AND CONTENT DEVELOPMENT PRACTICES WITH AI: A COMMUNITY-BASED WORKFLOW FOR AUGMENTING HAWAIIAN LANGUAGE ASSESSMENTS

bias_targets.methodology: Expert review of AI-generated interpretive briefs by Hawaiian cultural experts to detect misinterpretations of Indigenous worldviews, relational meanings, and figurative depth stemming from the models' primarily English-centric training data.

Qualitative evaluation by fluent Hawaiian educators to identify instances where the AI models incorrectly characterize valid Hawaiian grammatical features, nuances, and lexical distinctions as errors.

Using document-grounded language models to analyze and synthesize psychometric indicators, including Differential Item Functioning (DIF) flags and difficulty indices, to pinpoint structural and linguistic reasons why specific test items underperform or act unfairly for certain student groups.
